annotations.keyFindings: Each additional patient per nurse on nights was associated with an 11 percent higher incidence of category 2 or worse injuries; a float nurse was linked to fewer missed repositioning episodes.
annotations.limitations: Observational; staffing and acuity move together; cannot show that a fixed ratio prevents injuries.
annotations.notes: The retrieved evidence on staffing the board asked about.

annotations.title: Protected night repositioning rounds eliminate pressure injuries: a multicentre controlled trial
annotations.keyFindings: After protected night rounds, category 2 or worse injuries fell from 3.1 to 1.9 per 1,000 patient-days; rounds recorded on 84 percent of nights.
annotations.limitations: Uncontrolled before-after; new mattresses during the second period; incident-report counting.
annotations.notes: The change idea closest to the project.

annotations.keyFindings: 26 of 31 studies reported fewer injuries after bundles, but only five had a concurrent control; effects were larger when counted by incident reports.
annotations.limitations: High risk of bias; staffing effects not separated.

annotations.keyFindings: Incident reports captured 64 percent of injuries found at weekly skin inspection; reporting rose during improvement activity.

annotations.notes: Supports weekly inspection as the outcome measure.

annotations.keyFindings: Missed repositioning on 18 percent of high-risk patient-nights without a float nurse and 9 percent with one; float nurses available on 61 percent of qualifying nights.
Category 1 injuries were missed in 38 percent of patients with darker skin tones against 14 percent with lighter tones; touch-based assessment reduced the gap.
For fewer than two events per ward per week, charts of patient-days between events detected a halving earlier than weekly run charts.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Worse night staffing is associated with more pressure injuries, and a float nurse is associated with less missed repositioning, but neither study shows that a fixed ratio prevents injuries. Protected night rounds were followed by fewer injuries in one uncontrolled report. Incident reports undercount injuries found at weekly inspection, and early injuries are missed more often in darker skin. Rare events are better charted as patient-days between events. The multicentre ratio study quoted to the board was offered only as an unverified model lead and was not retrieved.
gradeRationale: Observational and uncontrolled before-after evidence, one review of studies at high risk of bias; consistent in direction, with serious confounding by acuity.
summary: Seven records appraised; four claims; the renaming of record 2 is refused; certainty low.
